fact: A World Bank-funded pilot in N'Djamena registers refugees biometrically in the SIGPTS and issues National Refugee Identification Numbers (NNIRs), with UNHCR hoping to expand to 25,000 IDs and eventually all refugees aged ten and above, per Biometric Update citing UNHCR.
More than 4,000 refugees in N'Djamena had received NNIR identity documents as of 1 May 2025, against a pilot target of 7,000, per Biometric Update citing UNHCR.
UNHCR, with ANATS and CNARR, launched at the Abeche guichet unique an operation to enrol Sudanese refugees biometrically into the national database.
The World Bank states that, with other actors, 25,000 secure identity documents have been issued to refugees to date, against a target of 80,000.
The World Bank lists coordination with UNHCR, CNARR and ANATS and the integration of refugees into the unified social registry (RSU) among the planned actions of the new project.
